findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/tests/external_calls.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The 'why' is one blanket sentence, not a reason for each commit; a declared intervention commit is not marked as one.
findings.evidence: Interventions are declared by an `Athena-Intervention: <id>` trailer in the commit message (crates/athena-gate/src/history.rs:226, 354, 441). The request asks land to name 'each extra commit and why'. The plan prints `<sha12> <subject>` per commit and then one shared reason. Fix: Have commits_after also return the message body, or check for the trailer. For a commit carrying `Athena-Intervention:`, add per-commit text such as 'declared intervention <id>; still refused until D111'. In criterion 3, assert that this text appears on Y's line.

findings.summary: Deleting replace_head leaves the dead force-replace helpers in place, so the plan's 'structural' guarantee covers only the Remote trait.
findings.evidence: gh.rs:1356-1374 is the only caller of check_replace and ReplaceRequest seen in this file. The plan keeps them, and Git::push_if_remote_at, as pub code. Fix: Either remove GitRemote's use of push_if_remote_at along with Remote::replace and say in the change description that the helpers are now dead, or delete them in this change if no other caller exists (check with grep).
findings.location: Risks: check_replace / ReplaceRequest / Git::push_if_remote_at left unused

summary: I read gh.rs, grepped the CLI and gate crates, and ran nothing. The plan puts the fix where the fault starts. In gh.rs:1297-1309, land_pr judges and merge-guards `link.head`. publish stores that as the job's commit, and replace_head (gh.rs:1356) force-pushes the job's commit over any different remote head. So a fix pushed to the PR is ignored, or worse, overwritten. Reading the current head with the existing `Remote::remote_head` (gh.rs:561) fixes this. So do judging and guarding with that head, deleting `Remote::replace` (gh.rs:566, 597 and the fakes at 1902, 2620, external_calls.rs:443), and refusing whenever head != job.commit. That matches the request, including the 'declared intervention or not' rule. The demonstrations would fail on the old code. The old code judges the stored landing sha, so it reports red, and it never refuses. A refusal returned as Err propagates through `?` in main.rs:759 and exits nonzero, so main.rs plausibly needs no change. Changing external_calls.rs is needed to compile, so Athena's scope finding is justified, not scope creep. No athena.toml field is added. The work fits one producer run. The two minor points: give each extra commit its own reason (mark Athena-Intervention commits), and tidy the now-dead replace helpers.
